coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 only (130–140 bpm), rolling terrain if possible. Your resting HR is 7.5 bpm above your 30-day average and recovery score sits at 46/100—both yellow flags that you're not fully bounced back from last week's 31.1-mile block. This is a taper Thursday; the goal is to keep your aerobic system engaged without adding load. Skip any tempo or hill repeats. If you feel flat during the run, dial it back to 5 miles and call it a win.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're 29 days out; fueling discipline matters now. Eat 1.2g carbs per kg bodyweight today (assume ~80kg, so ~96g minimum), split across 4–5 meals. Post-run, consume 40g carbs + 20g protein within 30 minutes to stabilize blood sugar and blunt cortisol after the taper stress. Your sleep efficiency (70%) is solid but not elite—consistent carb intake helps stabilize sleep quality. Avoid a large dinner; finish eating 2–3 hours before bed.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep was 8.3h last night—good volume, but 70% efficiency suggests fragmentation or light stages. Aim for 9 hours tonight and create hard conditions: dark room (0 lux), cool (18–19°C if possible), no screens after 21:00. Your elevated resting HR suggests residual sympathetic activation; prioritize sleep over anything else this week. Skip afternoon caffeine entirely. If you're traveling for work, a 20-minute nap (not longer) at 14:00–15:00 can help reset nervous system state without harming tonight's sleep.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the final 4 weeks; this is where doubt creeps in. Your last hard run (12.04mi @ 1457ft, Aug 13) was solid—hold that as your reference. The taper will feel sluggish for 7–10 days; that's neurological adaptation, not fitness loss. Use this Thursday to remind yourself that you've logged the vert, you've logged the miles, and now you're sharpening the tool. Visualize 2–3 specific sections of the course (the initial steep push, the ridge traverse, the final descent) for 5 minutes post-run. Trust the plan.
